toc.title: The exam, its scope and how this course works

html:
1What You Will Learn

  • Describe the exam: its length, its four question types and how it is scored
  • Say what the exam guide covers and why you should read the current version
  • Name the five domains and their weights
  • Know who the exam is for and what it leaves out
  • Use the tags, case, Design Checks and questions of this course

2The exam, its scope and how this course works

Running case

Meet Cedar and Salt Travel

  • Cedar and Salt Travel is a fictional online travel company with a small product team
  • Its leaders want artificial intelligence (AI) that helps customers and staff, without losing trust or control
  • Step by step the team adds a booking assistant, translated listings, review summaries, recommendations and fraud checks
  • Each module follows one decision: what to use, how to prompt it, how to keep it safe
  • Your job: learn what each AI idea and AWS service is for, and when to choose it

The Exam at a Glance

  • 65 questions: 50 are scored and 15 are unscored trial questions
  • You cannot tell which are unscored, so treat every question as real
  • 90 minutes in all: about 83 seconds a question
  • Your result is a scaled score from 100 to 1,000, and 700 passes

Exam tip: The 15 unscored questions are not marked on screen, so give every question your full attention.

Question Types and Scoring

  • Multiple choice: one correct answer and three distractors
  • Multiple response: two or more correct answers out of five or more options; you must pick all of them to get credit
  • Ordering: put three to five steps in the correct order
  • Matching: match every item to its prompt, from three to seven prompts; all pairs must be right
  • An unanswered question counts as wrong, and there is no penalty for guessing
  • Compensatory scoring: you must pass the exam as a whole, not each section

Exam tip: Never leave a question blank: a guess costs nothing and a blank always scores zero.

Booking, Taking and Keeping the Credential [Verify live]

  • Fee: USD 100, with possible extra costs such as exchange rates
  • Delivery: at a Pearson VUE test center or online with a proctor
  • Languages: several, including English; the Italian and German versions retire after 15 October 2026
  • Valid for 3 years; renew by passing the latest version of the exam or the Machine Learning Engineer Associate exam
  • No prerequisites
  • As of 5 November 2026: check AWS's certification page for price, languages and delivery

Exam tip: Fees, languages and renewal rules change; read AWS's page before you book.

The Exam Guide Is Your Scope [Dates]

  • The exam guide lists the domains, weights, task statements and in-scope services
  • This course follows version 1.2, published on 29 October 2026
  • The guide had three versions in 2026: 26 March, 30 April and 29 October
  • AWS publishes changes about a month before they reach the exam
  • The service list is non-exhaustive and subject to change
  • The guide outranks this course on scope

Exam tip: Read the current exam guide before you book and again in the last week.

Five Domains, Fourteen Task Statements

  • Domain 1, Fundamentals of AI and ML: 20%, three task statements
  • Domain 2, Fundamentals of GenAI: 24%, three
  • Domain 3, Applications of Foundation Models: 28%, four
  • Domain 4, Guidelines for Responsible AI: 14%, two
  • Domain 5, Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions: 14%, two

Exam tip: Domain 3 is the largest, but domains 1 and 2 together carry 44 percent of the exam.

Who the Exam Is For

  • The target candidate has up to six months of exposure to AI/ML technologies on AWS
  • It uses AI and ML solutions but does not necessarily build them
  • The focus is practical business applications of AI
  • Out of scope for the candidate: coding models, data and feature engineering, tuning, building pipelines, statistical analysis, and implementing security or governance frameworks
  • Task statements use verbs such as explain, identify, describe and recognize

Exam tip: Learn what each idea and service is for and when to choose it; building it step by step is not what is tested.

How This Course Works

  • 17 modules: this introduction, 14 content modules in the guide's order, a recap and an exam-technique module
  • Each content module has what you will learn, a Cedar and Salt case, Exam Tips, a recap and practice questions
  • A Design Check in each module, with orderings and matchings to practice
  • Slide tags: Beyond the guide, Old name, Verify live, Dates
  • Practice questions are choice questions; ordering and matching are practiced in the Design Checks

Independent Course, Official Sources

  • This course is independent: not affiliated with, endorsed or sponsored by Amazon Web Services
  • It shows no AWS logos or service icons; service names appear as text
  • The notes and questions are in our own wording; it uses no AWS exam questions or dumps
  • AWS documentation and the exam guide outrank this course on every fact and rule
  • Names, availability and prices change fast in AI: check the source on every Verify-live slide

Exam tip: When this course and the current AWS documentation disagree, the documentation wins.

3Quick Reference Card

  • Study one module, then do its questions; the modules follow the exam guide's order
  • Cover every task statement: the guide does not weight them separately
  • Read the exam guide before you book and again in the last week
  • Answer all 65 questions on the day; never leave one blank
  • This course is independent and educational: the official sources outrank it

Exam tip: Before you book, read AWS's current exam guide and certification page.
